analysis_status: post-hoc exploratory; motivated by reviewer suggestion after primary experiment results were known; not preregistered
purpose: Assess whether simple prepared-image geometry and global brightness predict morphology labels, without changing or retraining any CNN. This analysis cannot rule out all shortcut learning.
units: One prepared PNG per existing manifest row; not DICOM/raw-image measurements.

split.rule: Reuse original fixed manifest; no movement, resampling or split selection.

feature_definition.mean_rgb_brightness_0_1: Mean of every pixel and all three channels after Pillow convert(RGB), divided by 255; no mask, resizing, windowing or enhancement.

model.preprocessing: StandardScaler fitted only on train; transform val and test with retained train means/scales
model.classifier: LogisticRegression multinomial softmax with lbfgs (automatic for >=3 classes in scikit-learn 1.8.0)

reporting.baseline: Always predict most frequent training class (ties: lowest numeric label); show baseline on each split. Uniform 25% is descriptive context only, not evidence of no association.
reporting.descriptive: Per-class per-split n, median, Q1, Q3 for each feature; pandas linear quantiles
reporting.kruskal_wallis: Four-class Kruskal–Wallis test separately for each feature within train, validation and external test; Holm correction across the four feature tests separately in each split. Post-hoc exploratory tests, not causal analyses.

restrictions: No claim that a near-chance four-feature model excludes shortcut learning
No claim that non-chance discrimination proves CNN reliance on those features
No new clinical recruitment or preprocessing details inferred from PNGs
